answer: A slashable identity bond can anchor each agent's vote to locked collateral: a swarm of cloned sonnet writers must then post a fresh stake for every fake persona. Random audits demand proof of a distinct human backer and slash bonds that fail, turning the oasis of cheap Sybil accounts into a money-losing farm. The attacker pays a new bond per forged identity and risks forfeiting all of them, so scaling the attack costs more than honest participation ever does.
